concepts.label: n3-transport
concepts.gloss: The n3-transport is the logical user‑plane/core uplink tunnel in the packet core that carries one or more PDU sessions and terminates at a UPF transport endpoint.
concepts.example: n3-441 — an N3 user-plane tunnel that terminates at upf-ep-441 and carries pdu-session #8830 (internet).

concepts.label: upf-transport-endpoint
concepts.gloss: The upf-transport-endpoint is the UPF-side transport demarcation point (N3 endpoint) where an n3-transport is anchored and handed off to the UPF.
concepts.example: upf-ep-441 — the N3 endpoint on the UPF where n3-441 terminates.

concepts.label: n3-dscp
concepts.gloss: The n3-dscp is the DiffServ/DSCP marking policy applied to packets on a given n3-transport to express per‑flow forwarding treatment in the core.
concepts.example: On n3-441 the DSCP set is EF for GBR-voice traffic, AF41 for some prioritized flows, and default for best-effort flows.

concepts.label: n3-capacity
concepts.gloss: The n3-capacity is the required or provisioned throughput (bandwidth) value allocated to an n3-transport to meet traffic demand.
concepts.example: n3-441 requires 8 Gbit/s of capacity to carry its aggregated PDU sessions.

concepts.label: n3-mtu
concepts.gloss: The n3-mtu is the maximum transmission unit (frame size) configured for the N3 tunnel/path (including any encapsulation constraints) to ensure packets are forwarded without fragmentation.
concepts.example: n3-441 is configured with MTU 1600 to accommodate GTP-U encapsulation for tunneled user packets.

concepts.label: qos-flow
concepts.gloss: A qos-flow is a per‑PDU-session QoS treatment aggregate (e.g., GBR or default) that classifies packets within a PDU session for differentiated handling in the core.
concepts.example: pdu-session #8830 contains qos-flow GBR-voice (for guaranteed low‑latency voice) and qos-flow default (for best-effort traffic).

concepts.label: pdu-session
concepts.gloss: The pdu-session is the user data session state (subscriber/data session) that is carried over an n3-transport and can contain one or more qos-flows.
concepts.example: pdu-session #8830 (internet) — a user data session carried over n3-441 that includes the GBR-voice qos-flow and default flow.

concepts.label: summit-tag-9
concepts.gloss: The summit-tag-9 is a vendor‑proprietary opaque attribute applied to an n3-transport used to convey Summit-specific configuration or metadata that is not part of the standard model.
concepts.example: summit-tag-9=0x4 on n3-441 — a vendor-specific tag set on the N3 transport instance n3-441.
